newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM hopes for quick end to Northwest battle.
newsitem.headline: KLM hopes for quick end to Northwest battle.

text.p: Dutch carrier KLM said on Wednesday it hoped to resolve its boardroom battle over share ownership with U.S. partner Northwest Airlines within the foreseeable future.

"We hope to be able to announce a positive outcome from these talks within the foreseeable future, together with a good base for the further development of (the) partnership," KLM President Pieter Bouw told a results news conference.
However, he declined to give any further details of the likely timing, saying this could influence the conduct of the talks between the parties.
Bouw said a positive settlement of the dispute was inextricably linked to prospects for deepening the two airlines' highly lucrative partnership.
"There is an interconnectedness between the outcome of the talks and the achievement of a multi-year contract," he said.
But he declined to comment on reports the Dutch carrier was prepared to sell its 18.8 percent Northwest stake in return for a multi-year partnership agreement.
The two airlines have been locked in a long-running dispute over KLM's rights to a further five percent Northwest stake under an option exercisable in 1998.
Until now the alliance has been based on a series of one-year contracts, while longer-term contracts would enable the two to take the necessary financial risks to extend the partnership.

Finance director Rob Abrahamsen told journalists that over the past year the Northwest-KLM alliance, in terms of which the two companies operate as one on transatlantic routes, had generated increased revenues.
"The total transatlantic cake has increased and our (KLM's) share has increased along with it," Abrahamsen said.
Abrahamsen declined to detail how much revenue the alliance had generated for each of the two partners, but said their respective shares of the total had not changed.
